    11  /-!
    12  # Grothendieck pretopologies
    13  
    14  Definition and lemmas about Grothendieck pretopologies.
    15  A Grothendieck pretopology for a category `C` is a set of families of morphisms with fixed codomain,
    16  satisfying certain closure conditions.
    17  
    18  We show that a pretopology generates a genuine Grothendieck topology, and every topology has
    19  a maximal pretopology which generates it.
    20  
    21  The pretopology associated to a topological space is defined in `Spaces.lean`.
    22  
    23  ## Tags
    24  
    25  coverage, pretopology, site
    26  
    27  ## References
    28  
    29  * [nLab, *Grothendieck pretopology*](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Grothendieck+pretopology)
    30  * [S. MacLane, I. Moerdijk, *Sheaves in Geometry and Logic*][MM92]
    31  * [Stacks, *00VG*](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00VG)
    32  -/
    33  
    34  @[expose] public section
    35  
    36  
    37  universe v u
    38  
    39  noncomputable section
    40  
    41  namespace CategoryTheory
    42  
    43  open Category Limits Presieve
    44  
    45  variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasPullbacks C]
    46  variable (C)
    47  
    48  /--
    49  A (Grothendieck) pretopology on `C` consists of a collection of families of morphisms with a fixed
    50  target `X` for every object `X` in `C`, called "coverings" of `X`, which satisfies the following
    51  three axioms:
    52  1. Every family consisting of a single isomorphism is a covering family.
    53  2. The collection of covering families is stable under pullback.
    54  3. Given a covering family, and a covering family on each domain of the former, the composition
    55     is a covering family.
    56  
    57  In some sense, a pretopology can be seen as Grothendieck topology with weaker saturation conditions,
    58  in that each covering is not necessarily downward closed.
    59  
    60  See: https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Grothendieck+pretopology or [MM92] Chapter III,
    61  Section 2, Definition 2. -/
    62  @[ext, stacks 00VH "Note that Stacks calls a category together with a pretopology a site,
    63  and [MM92] calls this a basis for a topology."]
    64  structure Pretopology extends Precoverage C where
    65    /-- For all `X : C`, the coverings of `X` (sets of families of morphisms with target `X`) -/
    66    has_isos : ∀ ⦃X Y⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsIso f], Presieve.singleton f ∈ coverings X
    67    pullbacks : ∀ ⦃X Y⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X) (S), S ∈ coverings X → pullbackArrows f S ∈ coverings Y
    68    transitive :
    69      ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (S : Presieve X) (Ti : ∀ ⦃Y⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X), S f → Presieve Y),
    70        S ∈ coverings X → (∀ ⦃Y⦄ (f) (H : S f), Ti f H ∈ coverings Y) → S.bind Ti ∈ coverings X
    71  
    72  namespace Pretopology
    73  
    74  instance : CoeFun (Pretopology C) fun _ => ∀ X : C, Set (Presieve X) :=
    75    ⟨fun J ↦ J.coverings⟩
    76  
    77  variable {C}
    78  
    79  instance LE : LE (Pretopology C) where
    80    le K₁ K₂ := (K₁ : ∀ X : C, Set (Presieve X)) ≤ K₂
    81  
    82  theorem le_def {K₁ K₂ : Pretopology C} : K₁ ≤ K₂ ↔ (K₁ : ∀ X : C, Set (Presieve X)) ≤ K₂ :=
    83    Iff.rfl
    84  
    85  variable (C)
    86  
    87  instance : PartialOrder (Pretopology C) :=
    88    { Pretopology.LE with
    89      le_refl := fun _ => le_def.mpr le_rfl
    90      le_trans := fun _ _ _ h₁₂ h₂₃ => le_def.mpr (le_trans h₁₂ h₂₃)
